root_idea.summary: The root denotes inclination or deviation from a straight or upright state.
root_idea.development: Its uses develop from bending, turning, and curving of objects or directed movement to unevenness and deviation in land, paths, religion, scripture, and other abstract domains. Classical sources distinguish visible عَوَج from non-visible عِوَج, though some report overlap.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Quran-attested noun with a stable classical citation form and distinct Quranic applications.

senses.definition: Deviation, crookedness, or perversion from rectitude in a path, religion, or revealed text.
senses.usage_conditions: Used for an abstract defect or departure from what is straight, including seeking to divert or corrupt the path of God and describing a scripture as free from deviation.

senses.definition: Unevenness or irregularity in a level expanse or terrain.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of land or a surface whose variation is perceived by reflection or discernment rather than as the simple visible bending of an upright object.

senses.definition: In the construction لا عِوَجَ له: no turning aside from it, hence no evasion, escape, or way of avoiding it.
senses.usage_conditions: A conventional negative construction expressing that the thing in question cannot be evaded or eluded.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become crooked, curved, bent, winding, distorted, or uneven; crookedness of a visible or upright object.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The a-vocalized noun and related adjective are commonly applied to objects apprehended by sight, such as wood, walls, staffs, spears, and similar things.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Difficulty, arduousness, or a troublesome character in an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized application to an affair or matter, contrasted in the lexical discussion with the crookedness of a visible object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To turn or incline toward someone or a place; to come to, alight at, or pass by a place or person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of directed movement toward an abode or person and of stopping during travel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To remain, stay, dwell, stop, or pause at a place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used both intransitively for staying in a location and for stopping or pausing there.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To turn back from, revert from, or relinquish something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in expressions describing a person who does not withdraw from an undertaking or object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Returning to what one had intended, attended to, or been engaged in.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An infinitival noun reported for the act of returning to a prior concern or purpose.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To turn or deflect an animal or other object; especially to turn a camel's or horse's head by the rein, or to incline a head, neck, or tongue.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction may describe steering an animal, bending a body part, or turning something away from a direction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pay no regard or attention to someone's speech or discourse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional dialectal expression, with variant wording reported in the lexical sources.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone remain, stay, dwell, or abide in a place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb is used transitively as well as intransitively in this construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make, render, or cause a thing to become crooked, curved, bent, distorted, or uneven.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The causative use applies to an externally affected object and is distinct from something becoming crooked of itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bending, curving, and tension of the legs or sinews of a horse or similar animal; horses possessing this conformation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In descriptions of horses, the term may denote a recognized hind-leg quality and, by substantivization, the legs or animals characterized by it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To set or inlay a thing, especially a vessel, with ivory or tortoise-shell; an object so ornamented.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a specialized material and craft use of the Form II verb and its related passive participle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Pliable, tractable, submissive, or manageable, especially of a she-camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The epithet may also emphasize a soft, flexible manner of movement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Ivory, especially an elephant's tusk; also tortoise-shell and, in broader usage, certain bone material; a piece or object made from it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word can denote the raw material or articles made from ivory or tortoise-shell, including bracelets.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cry used to chide or urge a she-camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form varies according to definiteness, pause, dialect, and poetic usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An unsound or perverted opinion, saying, affair, natural disposition, or means of subsistence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of abstract conditions or character that are not sound or rightly ordered; the religious application is also found in broader traditional usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A species of millet or sorghum.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexicalized diminutive form used as the name of the plant.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A possessor or seller of ivory or tortoise-shell.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word is interpreted either as one who owns such material or as one who trades in it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexicalized feminine adjective used as the noun for the curved weapon.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bending toward a child to suckle; of a she-camel, lean, lank, light-fleshed, or emaciated so that the back is crooked.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The woman and she-camel applications are conventional specialized descriptions, not a general restriction on the root.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Oblique or slanting, especially of a new moon.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized astronomical description of the crescent's position or shape.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The days, figuratively viewed as alternating in their movement away from and back toward good fortune.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A proverbial pluralized expression for the variability of fortune.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A proper name of a watering-trough.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A named object rather than an ordinary descriptive use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An Awaji horse, or something related to the celebrated horse named أَعْوَجُ and its lineage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nisbah designation for horses descended from or associated with the renowned stallion; it is not a general adjective meaning crooked.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place to which one turns, or in which one remains, stays, dwells, or abides.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A locative noun associated with turning toward or remaining in a place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The act of remaining or staying, and the act of turning a camel by its head.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An infinitival use of the noun, with separate applications to staying in a place and steering a camel.

cautions: Classical sources commonly distinguish عَوَجٌ for visible or upright objects from عِوَجٌ for land and abstract matters, but they also report variant usage and disagreement over the distinction.
The Quranic form in this packet is the noun عِوَجٌ; the many derived verbs and adjectives in the Classical material are related lexical forms, not additional Quranic form groups.
Lane's printed Quran citations use historical citation conventions; the modern verse locations shown in the examples are taken from QAC occurrences.
